questions.explanation: 'Just' means a very short time ago and goes before the past participle.
'Ever' in questions means 'at any time in your life'.
'Never' means 'not at any time' and goes before the past participle.
'Yet' goes at the end of negative sentences and questions.
'Already' means 'before now' and goes before the past participle.
'Yet' in questions asks if something has happened.
'Just' goes between 'have' and the past participle: 'have just eaten'.
'Never' goes before the past participle.
'Yet' goes at the end of questions.
'Just' means it happened a very short time ago.
'Never' + past participle means 'not at any time'.
'Already' shows something happened sooner than expected.
In negative sentences use 'yet', not 'already': 'haven't arrived yet'.
'Ever' is used in questions about life experiences.
'Never' goes between 'have' and the past participle.
questions.q: I have ___ heard of that band.

'Yet' goes at the end of questions.
'Already' goes before the past participle.

'Already' in questions shows surprise that it's done.
questions.q: Have you ___ finished? The taxi is here!
